summary:
The SP category is the clear signal across every rating today — R1 through R4 all show identical 2-0 (100%, n=2) marks over the last 14 days riding 3-game win streaks, while bullpen_fatigue is the mirror-image disaster: 0-2 (0%, n=2) across the board with a 5-game losing streak on every single rating. That's a small sample, but the consistency across R1, R2, R3, and R4 all showing the exact same split is itself the story — this isn't noise in one model, it's a system-wide category signal. When today's slate has a game where SP and bullpen_fatigue point in opposite directions, trust SP and fade bullpen_fatigue as a standalone category. The season-long combo data backs this up structurally too: trends+sp leads all category pairings at 58.0% (370-268, n=638), so any game where trends and SP both back the same side is the sharpest play on the board today.

On the team side, if LAD or BOS show up as strong plays today, lean in hard — LAD's strong-play record sits at 28-7 (80%, +27.0u) and BOS at 22-7 (76%, +19.0u), both well clear of the pack. TBR (26-11, 70%, +21.0u) and MIL (29-13, 69%, +18.0u) are right behind them as reliable strong-side teams. Conversely, if NYY shows up as a model side today, be skeptical of leaning strong — their strong-play mark is a league-worst 9-14 (39%, -4.0u), the only team on the list actually losing money when the model likes them heavily. Rating-wise, the units P/L still favors R3 and R1 on season totals (+92.0u and +84.0u), but the 30-day window has R2 running hottest among the core ratings at 7-3 (70%, +3.0u), so if the board splits between ratings today, give R2 and R3 the tiebreaker over R1 and R4. Bottom line: hunt for games where SP agrees with trends, where LAD/BOS/TBR/MIL are the liked side, and where bullpen_fatigue is the lone dissenting voice — that's the fade.
